#367158 82 2007-09-24T01:36:58Z Condog
These are the other i liked:blaster drone, seeker mines, key drone, gold eater drone, pendulum, shock drone, heat drone, track, prism drone, confusion drone, blocker drone, bomb drone, platform drone, suicide drone, berserk drone


Heres my created enemies:

NOTE: for appearances, see attached doc.

1.Name: flame drone

Appearance: orange or grey with a flame on it.

Actions: like a chaingun except it shoots out flames, have a shorter range, the fire spreads a bit if it hits a wall.

Why: it would be cool

2.Name: Tesla Drone

Appearance: a yellow drone with a small rotating arm in the middle.

Actions: It constantly shoots out a line of electricity that rotates slowly in a circle around it. Stationary.

Why: To create a different kind of obstacle.

3.Name: Chemical drone

Appearance: green with a biohazard sign on it.

Actions: will shoot out gas if n is near, last for 10 secs.
If n moves through it, it will decrease his thime remaining.

Why: risk vs reward. if you can go through will enough time left, good for you, if not your dead.

4.Name: Proximity Blade

Appearance: A circular saw the size of a gauss turret with an antenna.

Actions: when n is within range, the antenna flashes and the blade moves towards n. It will continually follow n until he goes out of range.

Why: Yet another obstacle.

5.Name: Grenade turret

Appearance: grey with a green circle in the middle.

Actions: lobs a grenade at you. it bounce then explodes

Why: it would mean you would have to be on your toes.

6.Name: Prison Turret

Appearance: small grey octagon with an x in it.

Actions: if it sees you it shoots a ball at you, where it hits it create a dome that n can't move through, enemies can though.

Why: be careful or you be a sitting duck.

7.Name: Bounce Turret

Appearance: Like the gauss, except with an x on it and a small nozzle that follows n

Actions: Like the gauss, except it shoots lasers that bounce.

Why: They Bounce

8.Name: Exploding Turret

Appearance: The same as a rocket turret but with a black line through it, and the missiles have a red tip.

Actions: like a rocket, but it explodes when it hits, so n can't just miss it.

Why: it would mean you would have to be more careful around missiles.

9.Name: Mine Spawner

Appearance: A grey node.

Actions: two possible ways.
a. it shoots out mines every 5 second that stick to walls.
b. if it sees n, it shoots out seeker mines © - that follow him like rockets except slower.
Why: cave levels.

10.Name: Flipping One ways.

Appearance: One ways with a black circle in the middle.

Actions: every 5 or so secs they will flip 180 or 90 degrees.

Why: makes timing essential

11.Name: Copy Drone

Appearance: Red with oval black eye and an antenna

Actions: It only moves when N moves, and follows different algos, like it will move either the same way as N, the opposite way, or alternate ways.

Why: Would be great for puzzles.

12.Name: Follow Drone

Appearance: Grey with a red bar down the middle and an antenna.

Actions: It will move randomly until it view N, then it will follow the path that n is taking, to the nearest square.

Why: Would be great in cramped levels, would make it imortant where you step.

13.Name: Dynamo Drone

Appearance: A yellow drone with a black lightning bolt on it.

Actions: Shoots out a line of electricity that cycles between each compass point direction. Or it shoots both opposite ways at once and switches to others. Stationary

Why: To create another obstacle.

14.Name: Spider Bot

Appearance: a little black spider, same size as a floorguard.

Actions: walks on walls, floors, roofs, when it sees you it shoots web at you. if it hits you, you will be slowed for 5 secs. if it misses the surface will remain sticky for 20 secs or something, and will slow you down.

Why: be careful or you'll slow down.

15.Name: Electric doors

Appearance: a line of blue electricity in place of a door.

Actions: acts like a locked/trap door, but you can't touch it after/before.
open (d), or shut (e).

Why: adds difficulty because you can't touch it.

16.Name: Electric walls

Appearance: moving walls made of electicity.

Actions: you make a path for them, they follow it. they can either loop or go back and forth.

Why: can be used it puzzles, to make you race, or to make you think.

17.Name: Mirror Block

Appearance: Like a bounce block but with a shiny chrome surface.

Actions: Any projectiles bounce off it.

Why: Would create interesting situations

18.Name: Actual teleporters

Appearance: arrows on tiles pointing in the direction where you go.

Actions: one ways or two ways

Why: No more messing around with code.


And that is my enemy list.

i know it may be a bit late, and i know i am set down as a map maker, but i have a peom to submit:
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
What does the future hold?

What does the future hold for humanity?

Are we destined to remain unchanged, unevolved, oblivious to the turmoil and chaos thriving amongst the endless infinity of space?

Will we seek more, to discover the answers to all questions, to attain unsurpassable knowledge, incomparable wisdom?

Shall we rise, up and up, higher and higher, ascending through the destruction and despair, to take our place amongst the stars, victorious?

Or, will the unthinkable happen, that we become playthings for higher beings, that we end our lives in the cold darkness of space, alone and forgotten?

Can we resist our most basic impulses, strive onwards til the end of time itself, or will we turn inwards, and foolishly destroy our own race, our fellow man, in our folly?

But perhaps the most important question, the one that will break your mind, drive you insane with the answer to it, is this:

Would you really want to know?
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
enjoy!

Quote: Ditocoaf, November 18, 2007 02:28 pm
Idk... this is in the same vein as enemy-interaction; it doesn't seem to fit in with the style of N. Currently, there is no way that enemies can help you. To take it further: enemies don't do anything but kill you. (They have various ways of moving, and various ways of extending themselves to kill you, but the principle is intact: they kill you. that's it, no freezing you or doing anything else to you, no effecting eachother or anything else.)

This would create more depth to the game, but part of what makes N so fun is it's simplicity. The aspects of this game, taken in its parts, are very few, and very simple. It's the infinite combinations and arrangements, which create whole new concepts in themselves, that make it so big, and so limitless. Anything else added to this game would have to uphold that principle, and add to the existing patterns, rather than breaking them.

(The one obvious exception to this rule is if R&M decide to change a basic aspect of the game, and it's awesome.)

agreed. It doesn't fit with the style of N. N is a passive game where only you can get hurt. If you could destroy a door, what would stop you wanting to destroy everything else?

#18080 1 2007-11-22T12:33:15Z Condog
As of recently, i have run out of books to read. I have just finished "Six Sacred Stones" by Matthew Reilly (awesome!), and as i have already finished almost every single one of my books three times or more, i need some more stuff. I will be asking you to give me suggestions as to what books you have read that you think are really exceptional. I will make a list of my favourites, and will add others that people enjoyed.

***Please be serious. Don't suggest porn or toddlers books, say "i can't read" or "your a nerd because you read". There is a time and a place and that is not now nor here.***

So without further ado, here is the list.

Books/Authors Worth Reading

Matthew Reilly - all of his, but i recommend "Contest", "Seven Ancient Wonders" and "Six Sacred Stones". Full of non-stop action.
Phillip Pullman - "His Dark Material" Trilogy, probably the best i have ever read. Fantasy.
Douglas Adams - The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, The trilogy of five. (that's right, five). Really wierd, but hilarious. Science Fiction.
Garth Nix - The Old Kingdom Trilogy, fantasy, fantasticly written.
Steve Berry - "The Romanov Prophecy", "The Templar Legacy" and "The Alexandria Link". Has a unique style, revolves around historical events. Similar to Matthew Reilly, but more realistic.
Garth Nix (again) - The Keys to the Kingdom. For a yonger age group, but still enjoyable. Fantasy.
Paul Stewart and Chris Riddell - The Edge Chronicles. Really fantastic fantasy series. Also younger age group, but very well written.
Jonathan Stroud - The Bartimaeus Trilogy. Alternate Universe type series, but cool. Fantasy (sort of)
Michael Gerber - Parady books. Very funny. Did harry potter parodies, lord of the rings parodies, narnia, etc.
Eion Colfer - The Artimes Fowl Series. How did i forget? Science fiction, funny, actiony.

Any more i come up with, i will add to the list. Also, if you have a fav book, don't hesitate to ask.

#385206 29 2007-12-02T02:30:36Z Condog
Maraius watched throught the mist at the base on the hill. He could the see the Axxonist scouts walking warily through it, trying to locate any intruders.

"Traitor scum," he spat under his breath.

The scouts were spreading out now, into the mist, into the trap.

"Get ready," he said to his squad through his vox mike.

The hill was their objective. It was an essential vantage point, one that would be required as a strong base for their forces if the reign of destruction and torment was to have no end.

He could see the rest of the Axxonists in the fortress ready for the signal.

Just then, he could see the scouts clearly.

"ATTACK!" he yelled into his vox mike.

With a snarl, he lept from the cover and ran at the scouts, closely followed by his squad. The scouts barely had time to turn and begin to raise their weapons when they Maraius and his squad were upon them, hacking with blades and blasting with guns. Their end was quick.

"THE SCOUTS ARE DOWN! ATTACK THE BASE!" Maraius bellowed.

As soon as this was said, many things happened.

In the rocky outcrops opposite the hill, Morgran and his squad unleashed a withering barrage of missiles and energy beams upon the western wall of the hill's defenses. Within seconds it was destroyed in a blast of heat and turned to rubble.

In the air above the base, a large vehicle materialised. It looked like a large black shark, with angry markings, spikes and blades convering it's hull, and armed to the teeth with missiles and gun turrets. It unleashed a merciless rain of pain and death upon the helpless Axxonsists. Those caught in the open were instantly shredded in a whirl of pain and bullets. Those not killed ran for cover.

Out of the woods on the eastern side of the hill, a giant machine lumbered out. It looked like a massive person, but bulky and low to the ground, and in place of arms, it had huge guns. Without pause, it open fired on the defenses, and within seconds they were crushed.

Hundreds of men, all screaming and yelling horrible battle cries stormed out of the woods and the rocks and ran to the hill. With guns blazing and blades slicing, they stormed the base and hunted the Axxonists. Mercilessly they were cornered, and with no way to defend themselves, they were cut down in an instant.

Only when the last one was dead did the men stop. Their lust for carnage and death had been satisfied for now.

"WE HAVE WON! WE CLAIM THIS HILL IN THE NAME OF CONDOG!"

The battle had been won, and the hill was theirs. For now.

With the introduction of Unreality's speedrun mode, highscoring has suddenly become more appealing to me. So because i am starting to get serious about highscoring, i just thought i would make a place to keep track of my 0ths and innovations. Slashed 0th's are no longer mine.

0th's - Only counted on maps with 10+ people.
* 180-0 : Beaten by TFK. (damn!)
* 150-0 : Beaten by kk, then lookatthis, then TFK.....
* 136-1 : Beaten by niskin, TFK
* 172-0 : Beaten by xaelar, lookatthis, fenneth. Very nice run btw fenneth
* 153-1 : Beaten by TFK. Excellent run btw.
* 154-4

Innovations
* 180-0 : Used four wall jumps to get over the mines and land on bounceblock to keep speed.
* 141-2 : Used a corner jump instead of third wall jump.
* 100-3 : Beat drone to the bottom bounceblock and improved jumping bounceblocks.
* 150-0 : Under not over. Skimmed corners instead of jumping.
* 136-1 : Different route cuts of 20 frames.
* 172-0 : Instead of jumping up all the bounceblocks, do a trick to avoid jumping slowly up.
* 153-1 : Altered the route going up to the exit switch.

Filter -> Zig Zag :: Default settings

Okay, even though i don't have the game, this is the extent of my knowledge.

Up to four players can be present on the screen at once. Whether you help or hinder each other is dependent on the map and your current additude.

In survival, there is probably nowhere safe to hide, and whoever lives the longest wins.

In race, you are trying to do the level just like normal, but with more people. Some might require you to work together, i don't know. But yes, i believe some unscrupulous people just wait by the exit until someone else hits the exit switch.

In co-op, it is neccessary to work together. Mostly both players have to survive, one to get the exit swithc and one to finish the level.

Only one player needs to get to the switch to open the exit, and to touch the exit to finish the level.

As fo the bounceblock, i have no idea.

#423003 22 2008-03-29T05:39:05Z Condog
Here's what i got:

speed : the higher the number, the faster it goes. However a high enough number will result in the drone not moving, as it moves enough pixels to move to the spot it was in. As the number approaches this point, the drone will appear to slow down. As gets further away, it will speed up.

fireDelayTimer - no visible effect

prefireDelay - no visible effect

postfireDelay - no visible effect

laserPrefireDelay - no visible effect

laserPostfireDelay - The drone will remain immobile after it has fired for a varied time.

laserRate - no visible effect

laserLen - no visible effect

chaingunPrefireDelay - The drone will remain immobile after it has targeted, but before it fires for a varied time.

chaingunPostfireDelay - The drone will remain immobile after it has fired for a varied time.

chaingunMaxNum - no visible effect

chaingunRate - The rate of fire increase/decreases depending on the number used. As it approaches one, the speed will become faster, until it reaches a speed so fast it will immediately kill the ninja. As it approaches infinite, it will appear to lag between shots. As normal the shots will target the place where the ninja was when it started to fire. Thus, the larger numbers will cause it to be very unaffective, whereas lower numbers will result in a 100% death rate.

chaingunSpread - no visible effect

#431493 8 2008-04-25T08:57:18Z Condog
Matthew Reilly - all of his, but i recommend "Contest", "Seven Ancient Wonders" and "Six Sacred Stones". Full of non-stop action.
Phillip Pullman - "His Dark Material" Trilogy, probably the best i have ever read. Fantasy.
Douglas Adams - The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, The trilogy of five. (that's right, five). Really wierd, but hilarious. Science Fiction.
Garth Nix - The Old Kingdom Trilogy, fantasy, fantasticly written.
Steve Berry - "The Romanov Prophecy", "The Templar Legacy" and "The Alexandria Link". Has a unique style, revolves around historical events. Similar to Matthew Reilly, but more realistic.
Garth Nix (again) - The Keys to the Kingdom. For a yonger age group, but still enjoyable. Fantasy.
Paul Stewart and Chris Riddell - The Edge Chronicles. Really fantastic fantasy series. Also younger age group, but very well written.
Jonathan Stroud - The Bartimaeus Trilogy. Alternate Universe type series, but cool. Fantasy (sort of)
Michael Gerber - Parady books. Very funny. Did harry potter parodies, lord of the rings parodies, narnia, etc.
Eion Colfer - The Artimes Fowl Series. How did i forget? Science fiction, funny, actiony.


More to come...

#431608 21 2008-04-26T00:39:18Z Condog
1) Peripheral Vision is a prime example of a puzzle map. The gameplay, which involves dodging seeker drones amid a field of bounceblocks, some of which conceal switches, while others hide a more deadly secret, is addictive and challenging, always a good combination. And while it may seem impossible to determine which blocks are which, Evil_Bob has infact hidden the answer right before your eyes.
#431631 23 2008-04-26T02:55:43Z Condog
2) The Perfect map.
* Begin by combining two to five prime authors, mix well to produce Delirium.
* Add an idea, some innovation and a dream.
* Spread tiles generously and artistically.
* Add a train of drones, give them purpose and a path.
* Select the objects and enemies, give the ninja an adventure.
* Finally, sprinkle with gold, for a challenge and a treat.
The result? Sleeping with a Fish Named Eric.

EDIT: Here's one my sister did. She really wants a NUMA t-shirt.

Mt. Cliff is a map that is challenging and fun. Youll be addicted to finishing it and once you have youll be left wanting more. The placement of the bounce blocks are just right; it requires a skill to jump from each one. Never before have I been so intent on finishing a map; but this one kept me up all night. In the short run, its enjoyable and exciting; the exact features a map needs.

First off, i'm sorry for what you're going through. A few years ago, my great grandmother, who was in her 90's at the time, started to deteriorate so badly that she couldn't recognise ay of her family, not even her own daughter. And although she died of natural cause, and not the way your grandmother is, i still feel i can sympathise, as the person i went to visit was not the person i knew.

Personally, i don't think people in that condition should be kept alive. The kind of life, if it can truly be called that, that they must endure, as well as the people that love them, is not something that should be prolonged. Far better to give them a final release when they can still say goodbye than prolong their interment until they are a shadow of their former selfs.

One thing to remember though, is not to dwell on the bad things so much. Try to remember the happier times you shared with her. As long as you remember those, she'll always be with you.

#459477 121 2008-08-09T09:29:20Z Condog
I have a few forcefield drone variants you might like to consider:
* Gravity Pad : Works similar to a launch pad and a FFD combined. It sends out a constant stream of gravity (normal, anti or null, as determined by the power value) the width of a single tile in the direction of the pad. As soon as the ninja enters the area of effect, it's velocity is altered accordingly, but will not stop as it does when it hits a launchpad or a FFD. Would be able to edit the power, range of effect and direction.
* Force Beam Drone : Combination of a FFD and a Laser Drone. Acts like a normal laser drone, but instead of the laser killing the ninja, it acts as the force field does, pulling the ninja towards it. Doesn't kill on contact with drone. Editable properties included: power, range, pre delay, post delay, duration/

I know you've said it would be hard, but Ned could do with an overhaul. If you could alter the interface to include the updates to drones, etc, it would really help. Also, a tool to draw the path of enemies/objects would be awesome, as well as way to edit the properties of enemies/obects without editing the code directly, such as the power of launch pads.
